The trade-wind inflow of Invest 91W is producing scattered shower 
over the region. These showers are accompanied by 10 to 15 mph
southerly winds. Rain total are expected to be around 0.5 inches a
day through Wednesday night. With 91W moving northwestward into the 
Philippine Sea, conditions are expected to improve Thursday. Drier 
conditions are expected for the latter half of the week. 

Marine...
Gentle to moderate winds will prevail through midweek, then could
become light to gentle from midweek through the second half of 
the week. Seas of 4 to 6 feet will slowly subside, dropping a foot
or so by midweek. Deep southwesterly monsoon flow will keep the 
risk of scattered and isolated thunderstorms in the forecast for 
the next day, with the highest potential on Wednesday. Isolated 
thunderstorms will remain a risk through at least the weekend. There 
will be a moderate risk of rip currents along north and east facing 
reefs of the Marianas through at least Thursday. A moderate risk of 
lightning will continue through the weekend.

Tropical Systems...
Invest 91W is located near 12.5N 141.9E, (between Guam and Yap) and 
heading in a northwestward direction. This system is currently rated 
as high, Tropical Cyclone Formation Alert (TCFA), meaning this system
is likely to develop within 24 hours. This feature is producing 
widespread, locally heavy showers and isolated thunderstorms. This 
system is expected to strengthen over the next few days as it moves 
deeper into the Philippine seas. 

For more information on Invest 91W, see bulletins issued by JTWC 
under WMO headers WTPN21 PGTW and ABPW10 PGTW.

Eastern Micronesia...
Satellite imagery shows scattered showers across Majuro and isolated 
showers across Pohnpei and Kosrae. Altimetry shows combined seas 
between 4 and 7 feet across the region.

Pohnpei and Kosrae: The monsoon-like trough that has been situated 
across eastern Micronesia will generally remain north of Pohnpei and 
Kosrae. This will place Pohnpei and Kosrae on the edge of the 
stronger monsoon convection to the north and the surface ridge to 
the south. The current forecast calls for gentle to moderate winds 
with isolated to scattered showers and isolated thunderstorms over 
the next several days. Some uncertainty in the placement of the 
monsoon trough remains though. If the monsoon-like trough sets up 
further south, Pohnpei and Kosrae would see locally heavy showers and
gusty winds towards the latter half of the week. On the flip side, 
if the monsoon-like trough sets up further north, then shower 
coverage would reduce to isolated later this week. Currently, 
guidance has Pohnpei and Kosrae just south of the heavier showers and
stronger winds.

Majuro: An active weather pattern continues across Majuro. Scattered 
showers are ongoing across Majuro and Arno Atolls. Guidance shows a 
slight tapering down of showers and thunderstorms over the coming 
days as the focus shifts to the west. Some locally heavy rainfall 
and gusty winds will be possible tonight. 

Across the far northern Marshall Islands, widespread very heavy 
rainfall and scattered thunderstorms have been seen across Bikini 
Atoll. Strong gusty winds of 35 to 40 kt have been seen within this 
area of convection. This feature is expected to remain north of 
Pohnpei and Kosrae over the coming days, but will continue to be 
monitored until it exits the region. 

Combined seas are between 4 and 7 feet across eastern Micronesia. 
Combined seas will see minor fluctuations over the next few days, 
but will generally remain within the 4 and 7 foot range. Some choppy 
seas will be possible near heavier showers, but seas hazardous to 
small craft are not expected through the period. 

Western Micronesia...
Invest 91W is now the subject of a Tropical Cyclone Formation Alert 
from the Joint Typhoon Warning Center. No direct impacts from 91W are
expected across western Micronesia as the disturbance lifts to the 
northwest into the Philippine Sea over the coming days. Though, a 
monsoon surge to the southwest of the developing tropical cyclone 
will bring high-end scattered to widespread showers, locally heavy at
times, and isolated thunderstorms, to portions of Yap State and 
Palau through at least Wednesday. The highest shower coverage and 
thunderstorm chances will be at Yap. Please see the Special Weather 
Statement that was issued for Yap State and Palau for additional 
information. Shower and thunderstorm chances will begin fall back to 
mostly scattered starting Thursday night as the monsoon surge lifts 
northward as Invest 91W continues to pull away from the region. 
Mostly gentle to moderate west to southwest winds are expected to 
continue at both Palau and Yap through Friday with occasional gusts 
up to 30 mph possible at Yap, especially near heavier showers and
